title: Introduce elasticity-sentinel and provisioning-guard for Dedicated fleets
author: Evelyn Park
release_notes: Adds a non-breaking elasticity sentinel controller and provisioning guard to improve burst admission stability and reduce over-provisioning for Dedicated fleets.
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short-lived microbursts that lead to aggressive provisioning and subsequent thrashing between scale-up and scale-down windows. Those events increase cost and transiently degrade tail latency. This change introduces two cooperating components: (1) an Elasticity Sentinel controller that inspects headroom, recent burst signature, and inter-fleet spillover signals to provide an admission recommendation (Allow/Hold/Reject) for new burst commitments; and (2) a Provisioning Guard that mediates autoscaler-triggered grow decisions with short-term decay and a credits-based backoff to avoid oscillation.

Motivation: Current autoscaling reacts to instantaneous util spikes and a short smoothing window. That pattern can cause repetitive warm pool churn when several tenants emit correlated bursts. We want predictable throughput guarantees for paying tenants while avoiding constant cluster churn and excessive spot/reservation churn.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a sentinel-based admission path that checks a tenant's requested burst against a short-term modeled headroom and historical burst acceptance rate. If the sentinel returns Hold, the Provisioning Guard will defer autoscaler-triggered provisioning for an exponential backoff window and attempt an opportunistic warmlet reuse path instead. The guard also exposes metrics and decision traces so SRE and product teams can tune thresholds without code changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Sentinel controller and decision API
- [x] Provisioning guard with credits and backoff state
- [x] Metrics: sentinel_decision, guard_backoff_duration, guard_credit_balance, sentinel_rejection_rate
- [x] Unit + integration tests covering acceptance, hold, and reject paths
- [x] Documentation for operators and runbook entries
- [x] E2E throughput benchmark harness and artifacts

Design notes: The sentinel evaluates three signals: static reservation (committed capacity), ephemeral headroom estimate (5s median of available warmlets), and a burst shape fingerprint (recent burstiness score). The decision is advisory for soft SLAs and is implemented as a short-circuit in the admission path so existing autoscalers only consult it; we do not hard-block allocations by default. The Provisioning Guard retains a per-fleet credit counter; credits are consumed on provisioning and slowly replenish. If credits are exhausted, the guard prefers warmlet reuse and queued admission with best-effort TTL.

Telemetry and observability: New Prometheus metrics, relevant labels (fleet_id, tenant_id, decision), and traces propagated through tracing headers. Added a small console page under Dedicated -> Fleet Health to display sentinel history and active backoffs.

Testing and rollout: Feature gated behind --enable-elasticity-sentinel. Rolling canary applied to two low-traffic Dedicated pools for 72 hours, followed by staged ramp to broader pools once regression-free. Benchmarks included: synthetic-surge-5s, correlated-tenants-30m, and denial-backoff-replay.

Risks and mitigations: Incorrect thresholds could increase request queuing and increase apparent latency. To mitigate: conservative defaults, telemetry-driven thresholds, and an automatic bypass if average queue time exceeds SLA thresholds.

Related: ENG-2147 (fleet burst stability), ENG-2230 (warmlet lifecycle improvements), SUP-1023 (customer incident that motivated the change).
commit_summaries: controller: add Elasticity Sentinel with decision API and basic policy
autoscaler: wire sentinel consult into admission flow (soft advisory)
guard: implement provisioning guard with credit ledger and exponential backoff
telemetry: add Prometheus metrics and tracing for sentinel and guard decisions
docs: operator guide and runbook for elasticity sentinel
tests: unit and integration tests for acceptance/hold/reject paths
bench: add throughput benchmarks used in canary
review_comments: Ava Martinez: Can we document how sentinel decisions impact billing visibility? Suggest adding a debug metric for expected vs actual capacity allocated.

Evelyn Park (author): Added sentinel_expected_alloc metric and a short section in the operator doc explaining billing behavior. The sentinel is advisory and will not change committed billing unless explicit override flag is enabled.
Rohit Patel: The exponential backoff parameters look aggressive for multi-tenant spikes. Recommend softer defaults and a configurable fast-path for SLA-tier tenants.
Evelyn Park: Made backoff base configurable and added a fast-path whitelist by tenant tier. Updated tests to cover whitelist behavior.
Linus Ng: Can we add more state reconciliation safety for controller restarts? The credit ledger is in-memory in the first patch.
Evelyn Park: Persist ledger to existing fleet metadata store with an atomic update; added idempotent reconcile and tests for restart scenarios.
Ava Martinez (LGTM): Behavior looks good in canary; metrics are sufficient to tune. Approved for squash-merge after a small lint fix.
